title: Enterprise audit telemetry plays and HIPAA differentiation notes
body:
Purpose: quickset of messaging, battle-card points, and auditor-ready audit-log language that AEs/SEs can use when discussing SOC2/ISO/HIPAA readiness and telemetry expectations. Audience: enterprise AE, SE, CSE preparing for security reviews and procurement audits. Status: living draft — lean, pragmatic, testable claims, and concrete evidence to attach to RFPs/P-Card reviews.

TL;DR positioning (one-liners for slides/emails):
- For enterprises that need verifiable, exportable audit telemetry and configurable retention, Redwood delivers auditable request-level logs, configurable retention/export policies, and private deployment options that support chain-of-custody requirements.
- SOC2/ISO: Redwood operates with SOC2 Type II controls and provides continuous evidence (reports + access to logging exports and configuration snapshots).
- HIPAA: We offer BAA, private deployments (VPC/on-prem), and audit packages that map PHI flow to control points (ingest, KMS, access control, retention).

Key claims to use (concise):
- "Request-level audit logs available in structured, queryable format (JSON/NDJSON); exportable to customer SIEM or S3 with HMAC-signed delivery."
- "Configurable retention and deletion policies per-org and per-route; support for legal-hold and expedited data purge."
- "Private deployment option for chain-of-custody and air-gapped attestations (on-prem or VPC)."
- "Key management integration: customer-managed KMS keys supported for Dedicated/Private, with key-use audit trails."

Competitive differentiators (talking points + what to watch for from competitors):
- Redwood advantage: fine-grained, request-level telemetry designed for auditor consumption (timestamped immutable entries, request/response hashes, model-version, policy decision tags).
- Competitor pattern A (managed-only vendors): often provide aggregated metrics but not full per-request telemetry or easy export to customer S3/SIEM — call this out when customers require e-discovery or regulatory audits.
- Competitor pattern B (self-hosted runtimes): strong control but heavy ops burden and no long-term managed evidence (e.g., you still need to provide your own SOC2 artifacts). Position Redwood as the balance: managed evidence + private install options.
- Competitor pattern C (large cloud AI): good telemetry but opaque model-versioning and routing fallbacks; highlight Redwood’s model-version pinning and explicit fallback flags in logs.

Telemetry schema (recommended minimal set for audit-grade logs — include when certificate/controls requested):
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- request_id (uuid)
- org_id (redwood_org_id)
- actor_id (api_key_id or user_id)
- client_ip (redacted or full depending on contract)
- route (api route name)
- model_id
- model_version
- input_token_count
- output_token_count
- latency_ms
- host_id (instance identifier)
- plan_or_capacity_tier
- kv_cache_hit (boolean)
- policy_decision{fallback, throttled, routed_to_dedicated} (enum)
- redaction_applied (boolean)
- pii_flag (enum: none, probable, confirmed)
- request_body_hash (sha256)
- response_body_hash (sha256)
- audit_action (e.g., generation, embedding, rerank, edit)
- success (boolean)
- error_code (if any)
- retention_ttl_days
- region
- export_delivery_id (if shipped to customer endpoint)

Notes on redaction and PII: logs should include a redaction_applied flag and summary_count fields (e.g., pii_entities_count) but not store raw PHI unless contractually permitted; provide option to store only hashes of inputs/responses for forensic correlation. Emphasize that default hosted offering redacts sensitive content in logs unless a BAA or private deployment is in place.

Sample auditor-ready clause for RFP/contract (short):
"Redwood will provide immutable, timestamped audit logs for inference requests and related control events. Logs will be available in JSON format and exportable to customer-designated S3 or SIEM endpoints. Retention and deletion policies are configurable per-organization, and Redwood supports legal-hold requests and expedited deletion workflows. Upon subscription, Redwood will provide a SOC2 Type II report and, where applicable, BAA documentation for HIPAA-covered workflows."

Sample brief answer to common auditor questions (SE script):
Q: Do logs include full request/response payloads?
A: By default we log structured metadata and SHA256 payload hashes. Full payloads may be retained only in Dedicated or Private deployments or by explicit contract (e.g., BAA with agreed retention). We can configure per-route retention to keep inputs/responses for forensic purposes.

Q: How do you prove immutability?
A: Logs are written to append-only stores with signed delivery records; exports include HMAC-signed manifests. For Private deployments, we provide audit snapshots and signed snapshots of configuration and data flows.

Q: Can we push logs to our SIEM?
A: Yes. We support push and pull patterns: push webhooks, syslog, S3 export (with strong encryption and bucket policies), and direct integrations with Splunk, Datadog, and Elastic.

Evidence bundle checklist (what to attach to RFP or hand to auditors):
- Latest SOC2 Type II report (redacted where needed)
- ISO27001 certificate (if requested)
- BAA template and statement of applicability for HIPAA flows
- Data flow diagram mapping PHI paths with controls
- Sample NDJSON audit export (anonymized) + schema description
- Key management attestation (KMS logs showing key use for customer-managed keys)
- Pen test / vuln scan summary and remediation timeline
- Rollout/patching cadence and configuration snapshot for the last 90 days

Contract language snippets (short bullets that legal can copy):
- "Audit Log Export: Redwood will provide generated audit logs in NDJSON format on request and can establish automated delivery to a customer S3 bucket with mutual authentication."
- "Retention Controls: The customer can set retention policies at the organization or route level; Redwood will honor deletion/expedited purge within X hours of request (X negotiable per contract)."
- "BAA: Redwood will sign a BAA for covered PHI workflows and provide implementation evidence mapping PHI handling to controls."

How to position Dedicated vs Hosted in security conversations:
- Hosted: fastest path; includes SOC2 Type II, default redaction of sensitive content, and export hooks. Use when customers want minimal ops burden but strong third-party attestations.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): allows customer-managed KMS and network controls, richer retention controls, and per-customer compute isolation. Good middle ground for regulated workloads that still want a managed relationship.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): for full chain-of-custody, air-gapped requirements, or where customers insist on inside-perimeter evidence. Provide additional delivery artifacts (signed config snapshots, on-site attestation checklists).

Competitor callouts (quick):
- VendorX: aggregated metrics only; avoid claiming fine-grained telemetry when they only have sampling.
- LargeCloud: good exports but model-versioning opaque; push on determinism and explicit version pins in logs.
- OpenRuntimeY: self-hosted->high control but customers carry all audit burden; highlight Redwood’s managed evidence package plus deployment options.

Sample deck bullets for AE (one-slide summary):
- Compliance snapshot: SOC2 Type II + ISO-ready controls + BAA available
- Telemetry: per-request NDJSON, exportable to S3/SIEM, HMAC-signed manifests
- Controls: customer-managed KMS (Dedicated/Private), retention/expunge APIs, legal-hold support
- Deployment options: Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private (tradeoff matrix: speed vs control)

Operational notes for CSE/SE to implement play in deals:
1) Early ask: Does customer need PHI in logs? If yes, route to CSE for BAA and private/dedicated options.
2) During security review: provide sample export + schema + SOC2 report; offer a short demo of log export to their S3.
3) For procurement: propose 30/60/90-day retention defaults and show how to configure.
4) For audits: offer a live export and a signed configuration snapshot for the audit window.

Open questions / risks to surface with product/security teams:
- SLA for expedited deletion (X hours) — currently operationally handled case-by-case; recommend productize this into a configurable promise.
- Immutable store proof model: customers sometimes ask for cryptographic chaining (Merkle/log proofs) — feasibility and cost tradeoffs need engineering input.
- PII detection false positives/negatives: how to tune pii_flag and provide auditors with sampling evidence.

Next steps (practical):
- Validate telemetry schema with infra team and ship an anonymized sample export for AE demo (owner: Jon Rivera, due: 2026-02-28).
- Productize deletion SLA options and add copy to contract templates (owner: Sofia Nguyen, due: 2026-03-15).
- Create a one-pager + slide deck with the sample clause and evidence checklist for AE pack (owner: Maya Thompson, due: 2026-03-01).

Notes to self: keep this short and example-driven. Aim for a single auditor-ready JSON export and one contract snippet that legal can paste. Avoid absolute statements about competitor certifications unless verified.
